pages.text: One winter evening, Uncle Beppo was coming for dinner. Mom set a warm bean-soup pot in the big table's middle. Lulu stood on tiptoe and stretched a nose toward it.
Lulu could not wait and grabbed the ladle. "Me first!" Soup poured into Lulu's bowl. Silently, Mom pointed to the table end.
The chair there was empty. Uncle Beppo had not arrived. Lulu quietly set down the ladle, cheeks warm and pink.
The door creaked open. Uncle Beppo came in with his walking stick, brushing snow off his shoulders. "Our Lulu must be very hungry!"
He sat beside Lulu and held those small hands in both his. "Soup tastes better served together." His hands were big and warm. Lulu's long ears leaned gently forward.
He offered the ladle. "You serve. Me first." Lulu gave him a ladleful, then Mom. "Uncle first, then me!" The last ladleful went into Lulu's bowl.
Lulu looked inside. Served last, yet just as full. "Mine did not get any smaller!"
"Thank you for the meal!" All three raised their spoons together. The soup tasted better together. Lulu's blue bell jingled.
When the whole family gathered, Lulu handed Uncle Beppo the ladle first. "One, wait for the grown-ups to sit! Two, their bowls first! Three, one spoonful together!"
Uncle Beppo sat Lulu on his knee and hugged tight. Grown-ups served first did not make Lulu's bowl smaller. "Well done, Lulu! Uncle first, then me!"
